message.content:
Search this repository for the identity provider / SSO / OAuth abstraction layer. I need to find:

1. A package that defines an abstraction (interface) for third-party identity providers (e.g., IdP, IdentityProvider, AuthProvider interface)
2. Concrete implementations of that abstraction (e.g., OAuth2, OIDC, SAML, LDAP implementations)

Search breadth: very thorough. Look in directories like internal/, pkg/, server/, plugin/ for packages related to "idp", "identity", "provider", "oauth", "oidc", "sso", "auth".

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	package v1
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5	
6		"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
7		"google.golang.org/grpc/codes"
8		"google.golang.org/grpc/status"
9		"google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/timestamppb"
10	
11		v1pb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/api/v1"
12		"github.com/usememos/memos/store"
13	)
14	
15	const (
16		unmatchedUsernameAndPasswordError = "unmatched username and password"
17	)
18	
19	// GetCurrentUser returns the authenticated user's information.
20	// Validates the access token and returns user details.
21	//
22	// Authentication: Required (access token).
23	// Returns: User information.
24	func (s *APIV1Service) GetCurrentUser(ctx context.Context, _ *v1pb.GetCurrentUserRequest) (*v1pb.GetCurrentUserResponse, error) {
25		user, err := s.fetchCurrentUser(ctx)
26		if err != nil {
27			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Unauthenticated, "failed to get current user: %v", err)
28		}
29		if user == nil {
30			// Clear auth cookies
31			if err := s.clearAuthCookies(ctx); err != nil {
32				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to clear auth cookies: %v", err)
33			}
34			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Unauthenticated, "user not found")
35		}
36	
37		return &v1pb.GetCurrentUserResponse{
38			User: convertUserFromStore(user, user),
39		}, nil
40	}
41	
42	// SignIn authenticates a user with credentials and returns tokens.
43	// On success, returns an access token and sets a refresh token cookie.
44	//
45	// Supports two authentication methods:
46	// 1. Password-based authentication (username + password).
47	// 2. SSO authentication (OAuth2 authorization code).
48	//
49	// Authentication: Not required (public endpoint).
50	// Returns: User info, access token, and token expiry.
51	func (s *APIV1Service) SignIn(ctx context.Context, request *v1pb.SignInRequest) (*v1pb.SignInResponse, error) {
52		var existingUser *store.User
53	
54		// Authentication Method 1: Password-based authentication
55		if passwordCredentials := request.GetPasswordCredentials(); passwordCredentials != nil {
56			user, err := s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{
57				Username: &passwordCredentials.Username,
58			})
59			if err != nil {
60				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user, error: %v", err)
61			}
62			if user == nil {
63				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, unmatchedUsernameAndPasswordError)
64			}
65			// Compare the stored hashed password, with the hashed version of the password that was received.
66			if err := bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(user.PasswordHash), []byte(passwordCredentials.Password)); err != nil {
67				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, unmatchedUsernameAndPasswordError)
68			}
69			instanceGeneralSetting, err := s.Store.GetInstanceGeneralSetting(ctx)
70			if err != nil {
71				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get instance general setting, error: %v", err)
72			}
73			// Check if the password auth in is allowed.
74			if instanceGeneralSetting.DisallowPasswordAuth && user.Role == store.RoleUser {
75				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "password signin is not allowed")
76			}
77			existingUser = user
78		} else if ssoCredentials := request.GetSsoCredentials(); ssoCredentials != nil {
79			// Authentication Method 2: SSO (OAuth2) authentication
80			identityProvider, userInfo, err := s.resolveSSOIdentity(ctx, ssoCredentials.IdpName, ssoCredentials.Code, ssoCredentials.RedirectUri, ssoCredentials.CodeVerifier)
81			if err != nil {
82				return nil, err
83			}
84			user, err := s.resolveSSOUser(ctx, nil, identityProvider, userInfo)
85			if err != nil {
86				return nil, err
87			}
88			existingUser = user
89		}
90	
91		if existingUser == nil {
92			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "invalid credentials")
93		}
94		if existingUser.RowStatus == store.Archived {
95			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "user has been archived with username %s", existingUser.Username)
96		}
97	
98		accessToken, accessExpiresAt, err := s.doSignIn(ctx, existingUser)
99		if err != nil {

---

## Identity Provider / SSO / OAuth Abstraction Layer

This repository (github.com/usememos/memos) has a straightforward identity provider abstraction centered around the `internal/idp` package. The design uses a simple data-transfer struct rather than a Go `interface` with methods. Currently, **OAuth2 is the only concrete implementation**; there are no OIDC, SAML, or LDAP implementations.

### 1. Abstraction: `internal/idp` package

**File:** `/bench/repo/internal/idp/idp.go`

This tiny package defines the shared data type returned by any identity provider implementation:

```go
package idp

type IdentityProviderUserInfo struct {
    Identifier  string
    DisplayName string
    Email       string
    AvatarURL   string
}
```

This struct is the "return contract" that all IdP implementations must produce. Consumer code (the SSO auth flow) works exclusively in terms of `*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo`.

### 2. Concrete Implementation: OAuth2

**File:** `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`

The `oauth2.IdentityProvider` struct is the sole concrete implementation. It has two key methods:

- `ExchangeToken(ctx, redirectURL, code, codeVerifier string) (string, error)` -- exchanges an authorization code for an access token (supports PKCE via optional `codeVerifier`).
- `UserInfo(ctx, token string) (*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo, error)` -- calls the configured `userInfoUrl` with the access token and maps the JSON response to `IdentityProviderUserInfo` using configurable `FieldMapping`.

Configuration is provided via the protobuf type `storepb.OAuth2Config`, which contains fields like `ClientId`, `ClientSecret`, `AuthUrl`, `TokenUrl`, `UserInfoUrl`, `Scopes`, and `FieldMapping`.

**Tests:** `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2_test.go` -- comprehensive tests covering token exchange, PKCE, client authentication styles, context cancellation, and non-2xx userinfo responses.

### 3. Protobuf Type Definitions

The `IdentityProvider_Type` enum currently defines only one provider type beyond the zero value:

**File:** `/bench/repo/proto/store/idp.proto`
```protobuf
enum Type {
    TYPE_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
    OAUTH2 = 1;
}
```

The `IdentityProviderConfig` message uses a `oneof` with a single variant:
```protobuf
message IdentityProviderConfig {
    oneof config {
        OAuth2Config oauth2_config = 1;
    }
}
```

The API-level proto mirrors this structure: `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/idp_service.proto`

### 4. SSO Sign-In Flow

The SSO authentication flow is in the API service layer:

- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go`** -- `SignIn()` handles both password and SSO credential branches. For SSO, it delegates to `resolveSSOIdentity` and `resolveSSOUser`.

- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go`** -- Contains the core SSO orchestration:
  - `resolveSSOIdentity()` -- Looks up the IdP by UID, instantiates the `oauth2.IdentityProvider`, calls `ExchangeToken()` then `UserInfo()`, and applies the `identifierFilter` regex.
  - `resolveSSOUser()` -- Resolves or creates the local user from external identity info, including race-safe handling of concurrent first logins.
  - `getLinkedSSOUser()` -- Queries the `user_identity` table for an existing linkage.
  - `bindSSOIdentityToUser()` -- Links an SSO identity to an existing logged-in user.

- **`/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/auth_service.proto`** (lines 66-80) -- Defines `SSOCredentials` with `idp_name`, `code`, `redirect_uri`, and optional `code_verifier` (PKCE).

### 5. Identity Provider CRUD Service

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/idp_service.go`

Full gRPC/REST CRUD for identity providers: `CreateIdentityProvider`, `ListIdentityProviders`, `GetIdentityProvider`, `UpdateIdentityProvider`, `DeleteIdentityProvider`. Admin-only for mutations. Protects deployment-configured providers from being mutated through the API.

### 6. User-Identity Linkage (SSO account binding)

**File:** `/bench/repo/store/user_identity.go`

The `UserIdentity` model links external identity subjects to local users via `(Provider, ExternUID)` with a unique constraint. One local user may have multiple identities across different providers.

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_identities.go`

Exposes `ListLinkedIdentities`, `CreateLinkedIdentity`, `GetLinkedIdentity`, `DeleteLinkedIdentity` -- allowing authenticated users to manage their SSO account bindings.

### 7. Persistence Layer

The `store.Driver` interface (at `/bench/repo/store/driver.go`, lines 57-62) requires four IDP methods and two authentication config methods from every database backend:

```go
CreateIdentityProvider(ctx, *IdentityProvider) (*IdentityProvider, error)
ListIdentityProviders(ctx, *FindIdentityProvider) ([]*IdentityProvider, error)
UpdateIdentityProvider(ctx, *UpdateIdentityProvider) (*IdentityProvider, error)
DeleteIdentityProvider(ctx, *DeleteIdentityProvider) error
ApplyAuthenticationConfigMutation(ctx, *AuthenticationConfigMutation) error
IsRetryableAuthenticationMutationError(err error) bool
```

Three database driver implementations exist:
- `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/idp.go`
- `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/idp.go`
- `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/idp.go`

### 8. Deployment-Configured (File-Backed) Identity Providers

**File:** `/bench/repo/store/deployment_config.go`

Identity providers can also be configured from JSON files on disk (in `/etc/secrets/` by default), using the naming pattern `memos-idp-*.json`. These file-backed providers shadow database-stored providers with the same UID and cannot be mutated through the API. This enables Kubernetes-secret or environment-driven IdP configuration.

### 9. Authentication Safety

**File:** `/bench/repo/store/auth_config.go`

The `AuthenticationConfigMutation` mechanism ensures that the system never reaches a state where password auth is disabled for regular users while no identity provider exists (which would lock users out). Both IdP deletion and general-setting mutations are validated atomically.

### Summary of Key Files

| Layer | File |
|---|---|
| Abstraction (shared type) | `/bench/repo/internal/idp/idp.go` |
| OAuth2 implementation | `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go` |
| OAuth2 tests | `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2_test.go` |
| Store proto definition | `/bench/repo/proto/store/idp.proto` |
| API proto (CRUD service) | `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/idp_service.proto` |
| API proto (SSO sign-in) | `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/auth_service.proto` |
| IdP CRUD handler | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/idp_service.go` |
| SSO auth flow | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go` |
| Sign-in entrypoint | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go` |
| User identity linkage | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_identities.go` |
| SSO username derivation | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sso_username.go` |
| Store: IdP model + conversions | `/bench/repo/store/idp.go` |
| Store: UserIdentity model | `/bench/repo/store/user_identity.go` |
| Store: Driver interface | `/bench/repo/store/driver.go` |
| Store: Auth config safety | `/bench/repo/store/auth_config.go` |
| Deployment (file-backed) config | `/bench/repo/store/deployment_config.go` |
| DB driver: PostgreSQL | `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/idp.go` |
| DB driver: SQLite | `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/idp.go` |
| DB driver: MySQL | `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/idp.go` |

The architecture is designed for extensibility via the `oneof config` in protobuf and the type-switch in `resolveSSOIdentity`, but as of the current codebase, OAuth2 is the only identity provider type implemented. There are no OIDC, SAML, or LDAP implementations.
